definition: In this historical source, selfishness is linked with egoism and refers to a self-focused stance in which a person knowingly aims at their own benefit. It describes a pattern of putting personal gain at the center of one’s motives.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Egoism; pinned source text

reasons: The packet’s entry is for “Egoism,” not “selfishness”; it only cross-references selfishness, so the definition should not present selfishness itself as the sourced head term.

“Knowingly aims at their own benefit” and “personal gain at the center of one’s motives” overstate/paraphrase the source, which says only that egoistic attitudes have as their conscious end “the advantage of the personal self.”

The packet text defines **egoism** as attitudes/dispositions with the conscious end of the advantage of the personal self, and only *references* “SELFISHNESS” via “Cf. … SELFISHNESS” without defining selfishness itself.

The definition’s claims that selfishness is “linked with egoism” and that it “refers to a self-focused stance” where a person “knowingly aims at their own benefit” are not stated in the supplied packet.
No support in the packet for the specific phrasing/pattern claim that selfishness involves “a pattern of putting personal gain at the center of one’s motives.”
